newsitem.title: UK: George - Joining EMU at current stg level unwise.
newsitem.headline: George - Joining EMU at current stg level unwise.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Wednesday if Britain was to join a single European currency it would be unwise to do so anywhere near the pound's current level.
He added that some of the pound's current rise -- it has rocketed by more than 25 percent on a trade-weighted basis since last August -- was irrational.
"It's an impossible question to answer but if we were to join, it would be very unwise to do so at anything likely the rate we are at today," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee.
The British government retains an opt-out on membership of European monetary union, the first wave of which is set to go ahead in January 1999.
The pound jumped to a near-eight year high on Wednesday after a strong set of retail sales figures.
"I can't explain why it's risen to the extent that it has and therefore I am bound to assume that some of it is irrational, erratic," George said.
